Regular Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
Joint REGULAR Meeting
WEDNESDAY, MAY 11, 2011
6:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S.HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority

JOINT REGULAR MEETING
Wednesday, May 11, 2011
06:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.

None.

David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Serv/Deputy City Mgr
Tina Christiansen, Community Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Dir.

North Coast Rep Student Theatre
Matt Thompson, North Coast Repertory Student Theatre, stated that with the generosity of the City they did a play about the history of Solana Beach called "The Perfectly Perposturous Pirates of Solana Beach" that would run for one weekend, and he thanked the City for helping fund the production.
1.
Equinox Dashboard
Ann Tartre, Executive Dir, Equinox Center, presented a powerpoint (on file) and stated that they were an independent, non-partisan, not for profit research and policy center, that they were founded two years ago, that their main concern was how to accomodate growth in the region, that SANDAG figures stated by 2030 there would be an additional 650,000 people, and that they were producing an annual dashboard to provide some key indicators including water consumption, affordable housing, and land use. She said that water consumption was down 9% there was less waste disposal, and there was an increase in renewable energy consumption.

All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Development Review Permit (DRP) and Structure Development Permit (SDP) for 624 Mar Vista, Applicants: Tony and Jasna Frakes, Case # 17-11-03. (File 0600-40)
The proposed project meets the minimum objective requirements under the SBMC, is consistent with the General Plan and may be found, as conditioned, to meet the discretionary findings required as discussed in this report to approve a DRP and administratively issue a SDP.
Therefore, Staff recommends that the Council:
1.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing; Report Council disclosures; Receive public testimony; Close the public hearing.
2.
Find the project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Section 15303 of the State CEQA Guidelines; and
3.
If the Council makes the requisite findings and approves the project, adopt Resolution 2011-049 conditionally approving a DRP and an administrative SDP to demolish the existing residence and detached garage to construct a new two story, single-family residence and detached garage at 624 Mar Vista Drive.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Corey Johnson, Assistant Planner, presented a powerpoint (on file).
Council reported their familiarity with the project.
Mayor Heebner opened the public hearing
Ryan Gonzales stated that he approved the project and lived south of the project, that his concerns were addressed, and felt that the proposed changes would benefit the area.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Roberts to close the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
Councilmember Nichols asked why the placement of curbs up front was not included in this project.
Mo Sammak, Public Works Dir., said that he had discussed it with community members in the area and they decided not to leave it in and that they understood why curbs were requested but that they did not like the design. He said that he would work on some options and once a mutually agreed on curb design was reached that met engineering standards, aesthetics and functionality, it could be reviewed and it could always be removed if Council decided to do away with it.
Councilmember Nichols said that the application of curbs should apply to the whole neighborhood to be consistent by either having or not having curbs.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.

C.2.

0610-80)
Recommendation: That the City Council

Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, read the title of the ordinance.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.3.
22nd District Agricultural Association Community Relations Committee Update on Discussions with the City of Del Mar Regarding the Sale of the Del Mar Fairgrounds. (File 0150-85)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Discuss the item and provide direction to the 22nd District Agricultural Association Community Relations Ad Hoc Committee as necessary.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Mayor Heebner stated that the City was still waiting for a response from Del Mar regarding the matrix and Solana Beach’s concerns to review the public trust, that Del Mar had agreed with many of the City’s concerns and said that they would provide feedback, which was about 6 weeks ago and that no response had been received, and that there was a recent article in the paper regarding Mr. Hilliard looking into the Senate Bill by Yee.
David Ott, City Manager, said that Del Mar’s City Manager had stated that they did not want Solana Beach to think they had forgotten about it and that they still intended to get back to the City in writing and that they and had been busy, but would get back to Solana Beach on the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU).
Mayor Heebner said that all communications from Del Mar were coming through the newspapers instead of directly.
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding the MOU and that the elapsed time had staled the agreement, to consider telling them to not bother on the MOU, and to get back to the City on the matrix, which was an analysis of Del Mar’s recent proposal in January for governance and ownership providing some issues and a comparison between a potential JPA (Joint Powers Authority) and a Special District.
David Ott, City Manager, said that the 22nd District was interested in what Solana Beach’s issues were, that it was shared that the biggest concern was Council’s issue that no 3-person board or Council could change the structure, that it was an historical opportunity for the local region to control what goes on at the Fairgrounds, and explained that the City’s intent was to create something that would work.
Councilmember Roberts said that everyone should know that the Del Mar City Manager had resigned her positon and was moving to San Juan Capistrano, that he had a conversation with Kehoe and that the legislation was moving to a 2 year bill and that there were multiple options to look at, that the article was a complete surprise to the City since it was not notified, and that it was a time to improve the relationship with the 22nd DAA.
Mayor Heebner stated that she talked to a policy advisor to the Senator and there was continuing discussion, that SB1 was not completely dead but turned into a 2 year bill, that there could be a trailer added to the bill, and that there were benefits from the Fairgrounds as well as unmitigated impacts and costs.
Councilmember Campbell asked about Del Mar’s status with negotiations with the horseowner group ad their investment.
Mayor Heebner said that it was only known that there was not a MOU, but they had also suggested that they had an agreement.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the City had requested the status of any negotiations or agreement and that they had only confirmed that they were making progress.
C.4.
Fletcher Cove Community Center granting easement for erection of new utility pole anchor.
1. Adopt Resolution 2011-066 authorizing the City Manager to execute an easement with SDG&E for the placement and maintenance of guy poles, anchors and connecting wires needed to support a replacement utility pole that will be installed on the Fletcher Cove Community Center property, along Pacific Avenue, south of the community center building.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item
Mo Sammak, Dir of Public Works/Engineering, presented a powerpoint (on file).
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding the anchors which appeared thin looking but were high strength, to what extent these will impact the Phase 3 improvements in this area, the dimensions of the area and that they would be a slight expansion from the current anchors, that the only alternative option would be a steel pole that would be significantly more expensive, and whether the wire cover could be a different color to not draw too much attention to it.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Roberts.
Motion carried unanimously.
